advances: Necessary conditions at an attained fixed-fiber optimizer, with separate positive-mass and vanishing-mass contact alternatives.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
By 1ec728c26c11b368, $c$ is continuous and the minimum is attained. Capacity domination for all restricted caps is equivalent to the original ambient constraints. Nonvertical caps have the normalized form, and thresholds outside $[-R,R]$ are trivial or controlled by the all-$K$ constraint at $-R$. For a vertical cap containing $K$ first move its boundary to base $z_0$. If its margin is $a\cdot(z-z_0)$, then for each unit $u$ the cap $La\cdot(z-z_0)+u\cdot x\ge-R$ includes exactly the same sampled fibers for all sufficiently large $L>0$, including the full boundary fibers. Thus the capacity inequality at $(u,-R)$ also implies the original vertical constraint.

If the slack $s_G$ were uniformly positive over positive-mass caps, a slightly larger scalar multiple of $\rho$ would be feasible. Therefore the nested sets in the definition of $T$ have nonempty compact closures in $K$, and $T$ is nonempty. If $b\notin\operatorname{conv}(T)$, take a separating affine function $\ell$ with $\ell(b)>0>\sup_T\ell$. By compactness there are $\varepsilon_0,\delta>0$ such that $\ell(b_G)\le-\delta$ for $s_G\le\varepsilon_0$, since otherwise a sequence of such barycenters with slack tending to zero would violate the strict separation. Let $L=\sup_K|\ell|$. For sufficiently small $h>0$, the measure $d\rho_h=e^{h\ell}d\rho$ is log-concave on the actual affine support. Uniformly in positive-mass caps the conditional multiplier is at most $1+h\ell(b_G)+h^2 L^2 e^{hL}/2$. It is at most one for the nearly tight caps and at most $e^{hL}\le e^{\varepsilon_0}$ for all others. Null caps stay null. Therefore $\rho_h$ is feasible, while $\rho_h(K)\ge W(1+h\ell(b))>W$. This contradiction gives $b\in\operatorname{conv}(T)$ and the finite representation follows by Carathéodory in its affine support.

For the limit assertions, write the sequence as $G_j$ with convergent parameters, $s_{G_j}\to0$ and $b_{G_j}$ tending to the selected point of $T$. By continuity, $\rho(G_j)=e^{-s_{G_j}}c(u_j,t_j)\to c(u,t)$. Every weak limit of the unnormalized restrictions is dominated by $\rho$ and supported on the closed limiting cap $G$: compact sets strictly below its limiting threshold are eventually missed by uniform convergence of the margins. If the limit capacity is positive, the limiting restriction has total mass $c(u,t)$ and $\rho(G)\le c(u,t)$ by feasibility, so it equals $\rho|_G$ and $G$ is tight. If the limit capacity is zero, $G$ has $\rho$-mass zero, and the support of $\rho$ lies in $\{u\cdot x\le t\}$ since any support point with strict reverse inequality would give $G$ positive mass. The weak limit of conditional laws is supported both on the support and on $G$, by the same threshold argument. It is therefore supported on the asserted face. A normal perpendicular to a lower-dimensional affine support can make that face improper, and the argument does not identify a positive-mass contact in the zero-capacity case.

statement:
Let $\rho$ maximize the halfspace-dominated log-concave mass on the fixed fiber $K$ at base $z_0$ as in pk-w33-fixed-fiber-log-concave-target-attainment, with original measure $\mu$. Put $W=\rho(K)>0$, let $b$ be its barycenter, and let $r=\dim\operatorname{aff}(\operatorname{supp}\rho)$. Choose $R$ larger than the norms of all continuous coordinates of the sampled family. For unit $u$ and $t\in[-R,R]$ use the capacity
$$
c(u,t)=\min_{a\in\mathbb R^n}\mu\{(z,x):a\cdot(z-z_0)+u\cdot x\ge t\}.
$$
For $G=K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge t\}$ with $\rho(G)>0$, set $s_G=\log(c(u,t)/\rho(G))$ and let $b_G$ be its conditional barycenter; here a cap retains its parameters in the notation. Then
$$
T=\bigcap_{\varepsilon>0}\overline{\{b_G:s_G\le\varepsilon,\ \rho(G)>0\}}
$$
is nonempty and compact, and $b$ is a convex combination of at most $r+1$ points of $T$. For any sequence defining a point of $T$, extract a subsequence with limiting cap parameters $(u,t)$ and limiting conditional law. If $c(u,t)>0$, the limit is the conditional law of the actual tight cap $K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge t\}$. If $c(u,t)=0$, the limiting conditional law is supported on $\operatorname{supp}\rho\cap\{u\cdot x=t\}$, which may be an improper face in the ambient normal.
title: Finite limiting-contact certificate for a fixed-fiber log-concave optimizer
